toc.title: The Product Owner in the Events
What the Product Owner Is Not
Exam Traps and What the Exam Expects

html:
1The Accountability (CSM 1.4)

"The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team. How this is done may vary widely across organizations, Scrum Teams, and individuals."

The Guide does not define "value" or prescribe how the Product Owner works. It prescribes who decides: the Product Owner decides what is most valuable to work on, and the decisions are visible in the Product Backlog.

1.1 Product Backlog management

The Product Owner is also accountable for effective Product Backlog management, which includes:

Responsibility Where it is covered
Developing and explicitly communicating the Product Goal Topic 10
Creating and clearly communicating Product Backlog items Topic 10
Ordering Product Backlog items Topic 10
Ensuring the Product Backlog is transparent, visible and understood Topic 10

"The Product Owner may do the above work or may delegate the responsibility to others. Regardless, the Product Owner remains accountable."

Old wording

The 2017 Guide called the Product Owner "the sole person responsible for managing the Product Backlog" and listed "optimizing the value of the work the Development Team performs" among the duties. It said the Product Owner "may do the above work, or have the Development Team do it. However, the Product Owner remains accountable." The 2020 Guide speaks of accountability for maximizing value and says the work may be delegated "to others".

1.2 What else the Guide gives the Product Owner

Where Role of the Product Owner
Sprint Planning Ensures attendees are prepared to discuss the most important Product Backlog items and how they map to the Product Goal; proposes how the product could increase its value and utility in the Sprint; selects items with the Developers through discussion
During the Sprint Negotiates the scope of the Sprint Backlog with the Developers when the work turns out different, without affecting the Sprint Goal
Cancelling a Sprint Only the Product Owner has the authority to cancel a Sprint (if the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete)
Sprint Review The Scrum Team presents results to key stakeholders; the Product Backlog may be adjusted; the decisions "are visible in the content and ordering of the Product Backlog, and through the inspectable Increment at the Sprint Review"

2One Person, Not a Committee (CSM 1.5)

"The Product Owner is one person, not a committee. The Product Owner may represent the needs of many stakeholders in the Product Backlog. Those wanting to change the Product Backlog can do so by trying to convince the Product Owner."

"For Product Owners to succeed, the entire organization must respect their decisions. These decisions are visible in the content and ordering of the Product Backlog, and through the inspectable Increment at the Sprint Review."

2.1 Reasons (give at least two) Beyond the Guide

Reason Explanation
Clear accountability When one person is accountable for the value of the product, nobody can say "the committee decided". Success and failure have an owner
Faster, clearer decisions The Developers get an answer from one person instead of waiting for a group to agree
One ordered Product Backlog A committee tends to produce competing priorities and compromises. One person produces one order, which is the single source of work
No deadlock or watering down Conflicting stakeholder interests are balanced by one decision maker, not left in a negotiation among equals
A single voice for the Scrum Team The Developers and the stakeholders know whom to ask, and the Product Goal stays coherent

A committee is not shut out: stakeholders advocate and the Product Owner decides. The Product Owner "may represent the needs of many stakeholders" and listens to them.

Old wording

The 2017 Guide had the same rule: "The Product Owner is one person, not a committee. The Product Owner may represent the desires of a committee in the Product Backlog, but those wanting to change a Product Backlog item's priority must address the Product Owner."

Exam angle

an option that makes a steering committee, a vote of stakeholders or a manager decide the order of the Product Backlog is wrong. The best answer keeps the decision with the Product Owner and helps stakeholders make their case to the Product Owner.

3Authority and Collaboration (CSM 1.6)

The Product Owner has authority over the Product Backlog (its content and order) and works collaboratively with Developers and stakeholders. The Guide's rules show where each applies.

Subject Who decides How the others take part
Content and order of the Product Backlog The Product Owner Stakeholders try to convince the Product Owner; the Developers advise on feasibility and size
The Product Goal The Product Owner develops and communicates it The Scrum Team plans against it
Size of an item The Developers: "the Developers who will be doing the work are responsible for the sizing" The Product Owner "may influence the Developers by helping them understand and select trade-offs"
What fits in the Sprint The Developers select the items "through discussion with the Product Owner" The Product Owner proposes how the product could increase its value
The Sprint Goal Defined by the whole Scrum Team, collaboratively The Product Owner proposes the value; the Sprint Goal must be finalized before the end of Sprint Planning
Scope during the Sprint Negotiated between the Developers and the Product Owner, without affecting the Sprint Goal The Scrum Master helps both sides
How the work is done The Developers, at their sole discretion The Product Owner does not tell them how
Cancelling the Sprint The Product Owner alone, if the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete Stakeholders, Developers or the Scrum Master may raise the concern

Why this balance? The Product Owner needs the authority to keep the Product Backlog coherent and the product's value in one hand. The Developers need the freedom to decide how to build and how much they can do. The stakeholders know the needs. Collaboration joins the three: the Product Owner without the Developers' input orders items blindly, and the Developers without the Product Owner's order have no direction.

4The Product Owner in the Events

Event The Product Owner's place
Sprint Planning Takes part as a member of the Scrum Team: ensures attendees are prepared, proposes how the product could increase its value, discusses with the Developers which items to select, helps define the Sprint Goal
Daily Scrum Not required: it is the Developers' event. If the Product Owner is actively working on items in the Sprint Backlog, they participate as a Developer
Sprint Review Takes part with the Scrum Team; the Product Backlog may be adjusted to meet new opportunities
Sprint Retrospective Takes part as a member of the Scrum Team

5What the Product Owner Is Not

Misconception What the Guide says
A committee, or a role shared by several people One person
The one who assigns work to the Developers The Developers decide who does what, when and how
The one who decides how items are built At the sole discretion of the Developers
The one who sizes items for the team The Developers do the sizing; the Product Owner helps with trade-offs
The Scrum Master's manager There are no hierarchies in the Scrum Team
A gatekeeper who must approve every Increment before it counts The Guide gives no such approval role. Work counts when it meets the Definition of Done
Someone who can change the Sprint Goal alone during the Sprint The Sprint Goal is a commitment of the Developers; the Product Owner negotiates scope but does not change the goal
Someone who must approve that the Scrum Master or Developers may hold events The Scrum Master ensures events take place

6Exam Traps and What the Exam Expects

  1. One person. Never a committee, a board or a vote.
  2. Accountable, not necessarily doing everything. The Product Owner may delegate Product Backlog work but remains accountable.
  3. Stakeholders convince; they do not command. Changes to the Product Backlog go through the Product Owner.
  4. Developers size. The Product Owner does not set estimates; the Product Owner helps with trade-offs.
  5. Developers select the Sprint's items in discussion with the Product Owner. The Product Owner does not push work into the Sprint.
  6. The Developers decide how. The Product Owner never tells them.
  7. Only the Product Owner can cancel a Sprint. The Scrum Master, the Developers and stakeholders cannot.
  8. The organization must respect the Product Owner's decisions. If managers override the Product Backlog, the Scrum Master helps them see the effect.
  9. The Product Owner is part of the Scrum Team, not a customer outside it, and takes part in the Retrospective.
  10. Several Scrum Teams on one product share one Product Owner, one Product Backlog and one Product Goal.
  11. Old wording "Sole person responsible" and "Development Team" are 2017 terms. In 2020 the Product Owner is accountable, may delegate to others, and works with the Developers.

7Exam Q&A

7.1 Scenario questions (choose the best answer)

S1A senior director wants a feature moved to the top of the Product Backlog and approaches a Developer directly. What is the best way to handle this?

  • AThe Developer adds the feature to the Sprint Backlog immediately
  • BThe director makes the case to the Product Owner, who decides the order of the Product Backlog
  • CThe Scrum Master reorders the Product Backlog to keep the director happy
  • DThe Developers vote on whether to accept the request
Show the answer

Answer: B. Those wanting to change the Product Backlog do so by trying to convince the Product Owner, and the whole organization must respect the Product Owner's decisions. The Developers and the Scrum Master do not set the order of the Product Backlog.

S2A steering committee proposes that three managers jointly act as Product Owner, "so that everyone's interests are covered". What should the Scrum Master explain?

  • AThe Product Owner is one person, not a committee, and the managers can make their case to that person
  • BA committee is allowed if one member has the casting vote
  • CA committee may own the Product Goal, but one person owns the Product Backlog
  • DThree managers are allowed if they meet weekly
Show the answer

Answer: A. The Guide is explicit that the Product Owner is one person, not a committee, who may represent the needs of many stakeholders. Those who want to change the Product Backlog do so by convincing the Product Owner. Shared or casting-vote arrangements remove the single accountability.

S3The Product Owner has little time to refine the Product Backlog and asks whether a business analyst may prepare items. What is the correct answer?

  • AYes: the Product Owner may delegate the work to others, but remains accountable
  • BNo: only the Product Owner may touch the Product Backlog
  • CYes, and the business analyst then becomes the Product Owner
  • DNo: the Scrum Master must prepare the items instead
Show the answer

Answer: A. The Guide says the Product Owner may do the Product Backlog management work or delegate it to others, but remains accountable. Delegating work does not transfer accountability, and nothing makes the analyst a second Product Owner.

S4The Product Owner tells the Developers which person should build each item and in which order the tasks must be done. What is the best response from the Scrum Master?

  • AAgree, because the Product Owner is accountable for the value of the product and therefore decides who builds what and in which order the tasks are done
  • BAsk the line manager to review the plan, since the line manager knows each person's skills and availability
  • CCoach both: how the work gets done is at the Developers' sole discretion, and the Product Owner steers through the Product Backlog
  • DAsk the Developers to follow the instructions this time and raise the point in the next Sprint Retrospective
Show the answer

Answer: C. The Developers decide how to turn Product Backlog items into Increments and no one else tells them how. The Product Owner's influence comes through the content and order of the Product Backlog and the discussion in Sprint Planning. The Scrum Master helps both understand this.

S5In Sprint Planning the Product Owner arrives with a finished Sprint Goal and a list of items the Developers "must" commit to. What should the Scrum Master do?

  • AAccept it, because the Product Owner decides everything about the Sprint and the Developers must then deliver it whatever their own forecast says
  • BExplain that the whole Scrum Team shapes the Sprint Goal and the Developers select items in discussion with the Product Owner
  • CAsk the Developers to sign the list, so that every item becomes a personal commitment of the person who signs
  • DCancel the Sprint Planning and ask the Product Owner to come back with the stakeholders' agreement on the list
Show the answer

Answer: B. The Product Owner proposes how the product could increase its value, and the whole Scrum Team collaborates on the Sprint Goal. The Developers select the items from the Product Backlog in discussion with the Product Owner and decide how to do the work. A finished list handed down removes the Developers' forecast of what they can do.

S6Midway through the Sprint the Developers learn that one item is much larger than expected. The Product Owner insists that every item stays in the Sprint. What is the best action?

  • AThe Developers work overtime for the rest of the Sprint to finish every item exactly as planned
  • BThe Developers drop the Definition of Done for that item so that the planned scope still fits the Sprint
  • CThe Developers and the Product Owner cancel the Sprint together and plan a new Sprint around the larger size of the item
  • DThe Developers and the Product Owner negotiate the scope of the Sprint Backlog without endangering the Sprint Goal
Show the answer

Answer: D. If the work turns out different from what the Developers expected, they collaborate with the Product Owner to negotiate the scope of the Sprint Backlog within the Sprint, without affecting the Sprint Goal. Lowering quality or working overtime is not acceptable, and cancelling is only for an obsolete Sprint Goal and only by the Product Owner.

S7The company drops the product line that the Sprint Goal supports, in the middle of a Sprint. Who has the authority to cancel the Sprint?

  • AThe Scrum Master, because the Scrum Master ensures that all events take place and keeps the Sprint within its timebox
  • BThe Developers, because they do the work and see first that the Sprint Goal no longer makes sense
  • CThe Product Owner, who alone has the authority to cancel a Sprint when its Sprint Goal becomes obsolete
  • DThe stakeholders, because they own the budget and decide whether the work still has value
Show the answer

Answer: C. A Sprint could be cancelled if the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete, and only the Product Owner has the authority to cancel it. Others may raise the concern with the Product Owner.

S8The Product Owner wants the Developers to size every item as "small" so that more items fit in the Sprint. What is correct?

  • AThe Developers who will do the work are responsible for the sizing; the Product Owner may help them understand trade-offs
  • BThe Product Owner is accountable for the Product Backlog, so the Product Owner sets the size of each item
  • CThe Scrum Master sets the size of the items, because the Scrum Master is accountable for the team's effectiveness and predictability
  • DThe stakeholders vote on the size of each item, since they know best how much value the item carries
Show the answer

Answer: A. Sizing belongs to the Developers. The Product Owner can influence by helping them understand the trade-offs, for example by simplifying an item, but not by dictating its size.

S9Three Scrum Teams work on one product. Each team asks for its own Product Owner and its own Product Backlog. What does the Guide say?

  • AYes: each Scrum Team needs its own Product Owner, who orders a separate Product Backlog for that team
  • BYes, as long as the Product Owners agree among themselves how to divide the Product Backlog
  • COnly the Product Backlog may be shared; each team keeps its own Product Owner and its own Product Goal
  • DTeams working on one product share the same Product Goal, Product Backlog and Product Owner
Show the answer

Answer: D. If a Scrum Team becomes too large and is split into multiple cohesive Scrum Teams, they stay focused on the same product and share the same Product Goal, Product Backlog and Product Owner. One Product Owner keeps one ordered Product Backlog.

7.2 Recall Q&As

R1For what is the Product Owner accountable?

Show the answer

Maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team, and effective Product Backlog management.

R2What does Product Backlog management include?

Show the answer

Developing and explicitly communicating the Product Goal; creating and clearly communicating Product Backlog items; ordering Product Backlog items; ensuring the Product Backlog is transparent, visible and understood.

R3May the Product Owner delegate Product Backlog work?

Show the answer

Yes, to others, but the Product Owner remains accountable.

R4How many people can be the Product Owner?

Show the answer

One person, not a committee.

R5How can stakeholders change the Product Backlog?

Show the answer

By trying to convince the Product Owner.

R6What must the organization do for the Product Owner to succeed?

Show the answer

Respect the Product Owner's decisions.

R7Where are the Product Owner's decisions visible?

Show the answer

In the content and ordering of the Product Backlog, and through the inspectable Increment at the Sprint Review.

R8Give at least two reasons why the Product Owner is one person.

Show the answer

Clear accountability; faster decisions; one ordered Product Backlog without competing priorities; no deadlock; a single voice for the team and stakeholders.

R9Who sizes Product Backlog items?

Show the answer

The Developers who will do the work. The Product Owner may influence them by helping them understand and select trade-offs.

R10Who selects the items for the Sprint?

Show the answer

The Developers, through discussion with the Product Owner.

R11Who has authority to cancel a Sprint, and when?

Show the answer

Only the Product Owner, if the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete.

R12What does the Product Owner do in Sprint Planning?

Show the answer

Ensures attendees are prepared to discuss the most important items and how they map to the Product Goal; proposes how the product could increase its value; collaborates on the Sprint Goal.

R13How does the Product Owner take part in the Daily Scrum?

Show the answer

Only as a Developer, if actively working on items in the Sprint Backlog.

R14How do Scrum Teams that share one product relate to the Product Owner?

Show the answer

They share the same Product Goal, Product Backlog and Product Owner.

8Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Accountable for Maximizing the value of the product; Product Backlog management
Backlog management Develop and communicate the Product Goal · create and communicate items · order items · make the Product Backlog transparent and understood
Delegation Work may be delegated to others; accountability stays with the Product Owner
One person Not a committee; may represent many stakeholders
Stakeholders Try to convince the Product Owner to change the Product Backlog
Organization Must respect the Product Owner's decisions
Visible in Content and order of the Product Backlog; the Increment at the Sprint Review
Sizing Developers (Product Owner helps with trade-offs)
Sprint selection Developers select, in discussion with the Product Owner
Sprint Goal Whole Scrum Team collaborates; finalized before the end of Planning
Scope in the Sprint Developers and Product Owner negotiate without affecting the Sprint Goal
How Developers, sole discretion
Cancel a Sprint Product Owner only, if the Sprint Goal is obsolete
